entities.name: Sugar Boom and Slave Trade Expansion
entities.label: EventWindow
entities.summary: Following the Haitian Revolution (1791), Cuba replaced Saint-Domingue as the world's leading sugar producer. Massive importation of enslaved Africans fueled the sugar boom — over 600,000 enslaved people were brought to Cuba between 1790 and 1867, far more than to any other Spanish colony.
